result.own.banner.text: Being a carrier is common and usually does not affect your own health. This demo uses fictional results only.

result.pregnancy.chance.text: This is a chance for each pregnancy, not a prediction about any child.

result.overlap.formula.text: For autosomal recessive conditions, when both partners carry a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in the same gene, each pregnancy has about a 1 in 4 chance of an affected child, a 1 in 2 chance of a carrier child, and a 1 in 4 chance of a child who inherits neither familial variant. Each pregnancy is independent.

result.condition.illustrative.text: This label names an illustrative condition used in the demo. It is not tied to your real health record.

glossary.carrier.text: A carrier has one working copy and one changed copy of a gene for an autosomal recessive condition. Carriers often have no symptoms. A screening result describes what was found in the test, not a diagnosis for you or a future child.

glossary.couple-result.text: When both partners carry a change in the same gene, each pregnancy can be looked at separately. The numbers describe chances, not certainties.

glossary.diagnosis.text: A diagnosis is made by a qualified clinician using medical assessment, not by carrier screening alone.

glossary.uncertainty.text: Some results stay uncertain until more testing or counselling. VUS (variants of uncertain significance) are not used here to give child chances.

glossary.relatedness.text: Family relatedness can change how we think about whether a partner might carry the same change. Any added chance depends on the gene, the variant, and what is known about your family. A counsellor can put this in context for you.

glossary.options.text: People may discuss many paths with a counsellor, such as further testing, timing of pregnancy, or prenatal options where locally available. This platform shares information only; it does not choose for you.

glossary.next.text: Typical next steps can include genetic counselling, confirmatory testing if advised, and follow-up with your own clinician.

learn.carrier.full.text: A carrier screening test looks for certain gene changes. Finding a change means you carry it; it does not mean you have the condition the gene is linked to. Many people are carriers without knowing. Your own health is usually not affected for autosomal recessive carriers.

learn.carrier.short.text: A carrier has one changed gene copy. The test shows what was found; it is not a diagnosis.

learn.couple-result.full.text: If you and your partner both carry a change in the same gene, each pregnancy has chances for an affected child, a carrier child, or a child who inherits neither familial variant. The numbers come from a standard model for autosomal recessive inheritance and do not cover every situation.

learn.couple-result.short.text: When both carry the same change, each pregnancy has separate chances—not one fixed outcome for every child.

learn.risk-vs-diagnosis.full.text: Screening describes what was found in the test sample. A diagnosis is made only after clinical assessment. Carrier status is information to discuss with a qualified professional, not a label about you or a future child.

learn.risk-vs-diagnosis.short.text: Screening is not a diagnosis. Clinicians confirm what a result means for health.

learn.uncertainty.full.text: Tests do not explain every condition. Variants of uncertain significance, family history, and other causes may matter. When something is unclear, the path is to ask a counsellor rather than guess.

learn.uncertainty.short.text: Some results stay uncertain until more review. A person can help when numbers do not apply.

learn.relatedness.full.text: In some communities, couples are related. That can affect how likely a partner carries the same change. The added chance is real but usually modest in absolute terms and depends on the gene. Wording should stay respectful and non-judgemental.

learn.relatedness.short.text: Family relatedness can matter for partner risk. A counsellor can explain this for your situation.

learn.options.full.text: Couples may discuss timing, further testing, prenatal options where available, or other plans with a counsellor. This app lists topics people often discuss; it does not rank or recommend actions.

learn.options.short.text: Many topics are for counselling, not for this app to decide.

learn.next.full.text: After a result, people often meet a genetic counsellor, consider confirmatory testing if advised, and stay in touch with their clinician. Your pathway can move step by step at your pace.

learn.next.short.text: Next steps often include counselling and follow-up with your clinician.

ask.boundary.text: This assistant only shows approved content. A hard question goes to a person.

ask.handoff.crisis.text: If you are in immediate danger or thinking about harming yourself, contact local emergency services or a crisis line where you live. This demo does not place calls for you.

check.teachback.shared-chance.prompt.text: In your own words: if both of you carry the same change, what is the chance for each pregnancy?

check.teachback.limits.prompt.text: What does this result not tell you about a future child?

check.teachback.consent.prompt.text: Who can see your overlap result before it is shared?

check.feedback.correct.text: Thank you. You can review Learn again or talk with a counsellor to go deeper.

check.feedback.retry.text: Take your time. The pictorial choices are a rough guide—your counsellor can walk through the idea again without judgement.
